#
# gl_test case 214 (splitkick): kick 2's fragment job as Mesa 26.2.1 builds it
# on the drm-shim, cut from the pandecode trace of
#
#   tools/mali/drm_shim_ref.sh run <work> tools/mali/testdata/splitkick.vert \
#     tools/mali/testdata/splitkick.frag <out> --samples 4 --second-frame
#
# (gl_ref.py: a 64x64 pbuffer of the 4x RGB8 config, cleared and drawn,
# glFlush, drawn again without a clear, glFlush). The lines from its second
# frame's RUN_FRAGMENT to the end of its render target, the shader block's
# CPU address dropped (it differs run to run; two runs are otherwise equal).
# The program block is splitkick_preload.expect.json.
#
# The shim's Mesa lays the surface out tiled (no PAN_MESA_DEBUG=linear), the
# board reference linear (tools/cts/log/2026-10-28-splitref): RT 0's
# Writeback Block Format and the plane's Clump ordering are Tiled
# U-Interleaved, both row strides 0x1000 (one row of 16x16 tiles) where the
# board's are Linear and 0x100. Every other field equals the board's
# section 4.1, 4.2 and 4.6 words: pre frame 0 Intersect, Writeback MSAA
# Layered, surface and slice stride 0x4000, the plane 0x10000 bytes, the
# texture's sample count 4, the DCD's flags (Clean Fragment Write,
# Evaluate per-sample, Multisample Enable), sample mask 0xffff, the SPD's
# preload 0x3000. src/mali/frame_split_tests.rs
# (`the_second_kick_s_pre_frame_draw_reads_as_the_shim_s`) checks ours
# against these fields.
#
